name: City Centre and Ropewalks
tagline: Warehouse conversions between Bold Street and Duke Street
description: The grid of former rope-making streets now filled with independent shops on Bold Street, bars along Seel Street and loft flats in converted warehouses. Everything from Lime Street station to the docks is a walk away, and the area keeps a steady supply of short-let apartments.
bestFor: Nomads who want to land, walk everywhere and never think about transport.
pros: Walk to station, docks, shops and bars
Bold Street is the city's best independent strip
cons: Loud until late on weekend nights
Flats are small with little storage
Streets get messy after closing time

name: Baltic Triangle
tagline: Old warehouses turned into studios, breweries and coworking
description: A former industrial quarter south of the centre now holding creative agencies, coworking spaces, breweries, street food yards and music venues in raw brick warehouses. New apartment blocks have filled the gaps. It is where Liverpool's freelancers and tech workers actually spend their days.
bestFor: Freelancers and founders who want coworking and a creative crowd on the doorstep.
pros: Densest cluster of coworking and studios
Good food halls, breweries and gigs
Ten minute walk into the centre
cons: Club nights make weekends genuinely loud
Still patchy, with car parks and building sites

name: Georgian Quarter
tagline: Hope Street terraces between the two cathedrals
description: Liverpool's handsomest streets, a grid of Georgian townhouses running from the Anglican Cathedral to the Metropolitan, with Hope Street's restaurants, the Philharmonic Hall and the university at the edges. Flats are usually conversions inside period houses, and the centre is ten minutes downhill.
bestFor: Nomads who want period character and good restaurants without leaving the centre.
pros: Strong restaurant and theatre scene on Hope Street
Walking distance to the city centre
cons: Period conversions can be draughty and dear to heat
Student flats push up noise near the university
Street parking is difficult and permit-controlled

name: Sefton Park and Aigburth
tagline: Leafy south Liverpool around a Victorian park
description: The area circling Sefton Park's 200 acres of meadow, lake and palm house, spilling into Lark Lane's cafes and bars and the Victorian villas of Aigburth. It attracts professionals and families, and the riverside path at Otterspool is a short walk further south.
bestFor: Longer-stay workers who want green space, cafes and calm streets.
pros: Huge park for runs and breaks
Lark Lane packed with independent cafes
cons: Twenty-five minute bus into the centre
Higher rents than most of the city
Limited late transport back at night

name: Wavertree
tagline: Cheap terraces east of the centre with a huge playing field
description: An ordinary residential district of Victorian terraces around Picton Road and High Street, with Wavertree Playground, a retail park and the Liverpool Science Park nearby. Rents sit well below the centre and buses run constantly along Smithdown Road into town.
bestFor: Budget nomads staying a month or more who are happy to bus into town.
pros: Some of the cheapest rents in the city
Big green playing fields and cheap gyms
cons: Little to do in the evenings locally
Some streets are rundown with visible neglect
Petty crime rates above the city average
